scope: Separate Resolve workflow research pass based on nine DaVinci Resolve tutorial videos. This is not an extension of docs/editorial-grammar-upgrade-plan.md and does not implement product changes.

north_star.goal: Build an agent editor that can produce edits with the judgment, craft, and technical range of a professional video editor for users who are not professional editors.
north_star.not_the_goal: Do not clone DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, or Final Cut as UI products. They are references for professional editing capability, task coverage, and decision quality.
north_star.product_thesis: A user should be able to ask for an outcome in ordinary language and have Awidat inspect the footage, make professional editorial decisions, perform the required technical operations, explain/review the result, and render a deliverable.
north_star.sequencing_principle: Do not try to build the full autonomous decision layer before the professional editing substrate exists. First map and build the pipeline components professional editors rely on; then the decision layer can orchestrate them with enough tools and evidence.
reference_editors_are_useful_because: They reveal the complete set of tasks professional editors routinely perform.
They expose workflow categories Awidat must support internally: media organization, assembly, compositing, color, audio, motion graphics, and delivery.

They show the decision points a professional makes: what to keep, what to remove, when to cut, how to hide problems, how to preserve continuity, how to polish sound/color, and when an effect is justified.
agent_requirements: Understand editorial goals, audience, format, platform, style, and constraints.
Inspect source footage and indexed evidence before deciding.
Plan edits at the level of story, rhythm, continuity, visual clarity, audio polish, color consistency, graphics, and delivery.
Choose professional operations autonomously, not merely expose manual controls.
Persist intent and evidence so the user and future agents can understand why an edit was made.
Present reviewable proposals and final outputs without requiring the user to know professional editing terminology.
north_star.success_measure: Awidat is succeeding when a non-editor can request a polished video outcome and get a result that a professional editor would recognize as technically clean, intentional, paced, watchable, and deliverable.

method.video_capture: Collected YouTube metadata and available English caption tracks with yt-dlp 2026.03.17. Captions were used for notes and theme extraction; full verbatim transcripts are not stored in this artifact.
method.codebase_review: Read Awidat README, desktop README, protocol metadata, EDL operations, effect registry, render planner, indexer defaults, Python indexer docs/tests, desktop timeline, media, properties, transcript, notes, and action bar surfaces.
method.evidence_quality: All listed videos exposed English captions. Some were auto captions and should be treated as high-level evidence rather than exact wording.

sources.title: Introduction to DaVinci Resolve - [Full Course] for Beginners (2026)
notes: Resolve teaches the editor as a sequence of dedicated pages: Media for import and organization, Cut/Edit for timeline assembly, Fusion for compositing, Color for grading, Fairlight for audio, and Deliver for output.
The Media Page workflow emphasizes media pool structure, bins, clip metadata, preview, import, organization, and preparing assets before timeline work.
The Edit Page centers on timeline assembly, trimming, cutting, inspector controls, transitions, effects, sync, and clip properties.
The Cut Page is positioned as a faster assembly surface, separate from the heavier Edit Page.
Fusion is presented as node-based compositing with masks, merges, text, tracking, and procedural control.
Color and Fairlight are full workspaces rather than single controls: color nodes/scopes/grades and audio mixing/repair/export decisions are part of the expected editor mental model.
Deliver is a named final workflow with export settings and render choices, not just a button.

sources.title: Intro to VFX for Short Films in Fusion [FULL COURSE - Resolve 19]
notes: Short-film VFX is taught as a graph of nodes, not as a flat list of clip effects.
Common operations include media import, bins, timeline selection, opening a shot in Fusion, merge nodes, trackers, masks, mattes, and color/grade adjustments for integration.
Workflow often moves between Edit Page context and Fusion internals: the shot lives on a timeline, but its VFX recipe lives in a node graph.
The tutorial reinforces that realistic VFX depends on matching motion, masks, color, sharpness, grain, and timing, not just overlaying an asset.

sources.title: The Art of Invisible VFX in DaVinci Resolve - Full Fusion VFX Course for FREE!
notes: Invisible VFX work repeatedly combines tracking, masking, still-image patches, color matching, haze/rain/texture integration, grain, lens blur, and final detail passes.
The chapter structure shows an iterative shot-repair loop: set up the project, isolate regions, track movement, build masks/mattes, match the insert, and review the finished shot.
Color matching is treated as an integration requirement for VFX inserts, not only a final grade.
Several operations need reusable structured evidence: mask shapes, tracking data, matte behavior, match reference, and integration notes.

sources.title: Make Your Own Motion Graphics in Resolve! - HUGE FREE Workshop for Beginners
notes: Motion graphics in Resolve span Edit Page titles plus Fusion compositions with reusable node setups.
The workflow depends on keyframes, spline/easing control, reusable comp duplicates, masks/alpha channels, parallax, textures, particles, and 3D object animation.
Resolve gives creators both quick title controls and deeper procedural motion design when needed.
Reusable graphics behave like editable compositions, not just burned-in media.

sources.title: Everything You Need to Start Using Fusion [in 56 Mins] - DaVinci Resolve 19 Beginner Fusion Tutorial
notes: Fusion is introduced around explicit node concepts: media inputs, backgrounds, text, merge nodes, masks, inspector-adjusted parameters, and output nodes.
The learning burden is not a single effect; it is understanding data flow through the graph.
A practical editor needs to inspect what each node receives, changes, and sends forward.

sources.title: RESOLVE 18 CRASH COURSE - Davinci Resolve 18 Walkthrough [BEGINNER]
notes: A second beginner walkthrough confirms the same page-based mental model from the full course.
The Media Pool, bins, metadata, inspector, timeline, trim/cut actions, Fusion nodes, Color Page, Fairlight, and Deliver are treated as core editor concepts.
Resolve beginners are expected to learn where a task belongs, then use the page-specific controls.

sources.title: Why Your Color Grades Don't MATCH (And How To Fix It)
notes: Matching color grades is presented as a workflow problem: color management, reference stills, consistent starting state, shot-to-shot matching, and avoiding late-stage surprises.
The tutorial emphasizes resetting grades/nodes, comparing references, using stills/presets, and checking whether clips match before render pressure.
For Awidat this points to reviewable color-match recommendations, visual comparison packs, and grade consistency state, not only per-clip sliders.

sources.title: All the Ways to MOTION TRACK in DaVinci Resolve!
notes: Tracking in Resolve is not one feature; common categories include basic point tracking, planar tracking, surface tracking, and 3D tracking.
Tracked data is used to attach text or graphics, replace/patch surfaces, drive masks, and align elements to camera or object movement.
A useful agent-native equivalent needs tracker sidecars, confidence, tracked region identity, and operations that can bind overlays/effects to a track.

sources.title: HOW TO ANIMATE TEXT IN RESOLVE 17 - DaVinci Resolve Basics Tutorial
notes: Even a short text tutorial expects inspector controls, timeline timing, keyframed properties, tracking/spacing changes, dynamic zoom, and write-on style animation.
Awidat's title system should eventually separate simple presets from deeper property animation.

resolve_workflow_model.label: Media organization before editing
resolve_workflow_model.resolve_pattern: Editors import assets into a media pool, organize bins, review metadata, create timelines, and prepare media before detailed timeline work.
resolve_workflow_model.agent_native_interpretation: Awidat needs source organization metadata that agents can query and mutate: bins, labels, roles, tags, source provenance, proxy state, sync groups, and readiness status.

resolve_workflow_model.label: Timeline assembly and trim surface
resolve_workflow_model.resolve_pattern: Editors use cut/edit pages for trimming, splitting, moving, ripple behavior, transitions, inspector changes, and fast assembly.
resolve_workflow_model.agent_native_interpretation: Awidat should preserve its EDL-first model but expose richer trim modes, boundary tools, keyboard-level operations, markers, and clear proposal previews.

resolve_workflow_model.label: Inspector plus keyframes
resolve_workflow_model.resolve_pattern: Clip, title, transform, text, audio, and effect properties are adjusted in an inspector and animated over time with keyframes/easing.
resolve_workflow_model.agent_native_interpretation: Awidat needs a general parameter animation model rather than hard-coded title animation enums only.

resolve_workflow_model.label: Node-based compositing
resolve_workflow_model.resolve_pattern: Fusion work is a node graph with media in/out, merges, transforms, masks, mattes, trackers, text, particles, and 3D.
resolve_workflow_model.agent_native_interpretation: Awidat does not need to copy Fusion immediately, but it needs a graph representation for multi-step visual effects that cannot be represented as one flat FFmpeg effect.

resolve_workflow_model.label: Tracking, masks, and mattes
resolve_workflow_model.resolve_pattern: Tracking and masking underpin tracked text, object replacement, invisible VFX, patching, roto, and integration.
resolve_workflow_model.agent_native_interpretation: Awidat should add sidecars for point/planar/surface tracks, mask regions, matte confidence, and operations that bind overlays/effects to those tracks.

resolve_workflow_model.label: Color matching and grade state
resolve_workflow_model.resolve_pattern: Color workflows use color management, nodes, scopes, reference stills, shot matching, LUTs, and consistency checks.
resolve_workflow_model.agent_native_interpretation: Awidat should turn color-analysis into reviewable match plans with reference stills, scopes, scene groups, grade stacks, and before/after packs.

resolve_workflow_model.label: Audio finishing
resolve_workflow_model.resolve_pattern: Fairlight provides mixer, EQ, compression, noise repair, levels, loudness, and track-focused controls.
resolve_workflow_model.agent_native_interpretation: Awidat already has strong primitives but needs a mixer-grade UI, automation lanes, meters, bus roles, and audible review packages.

resolve_workflow_model.label: Delivery as a workflow
resolve_workflow_model.resolve_pattern: Deliver is a final workspace with presets, render settings, output validation, and render queue expectations.
resolve_workflow_model.agent_native_interpretation: Awidat's export path should grow into delivery profiles, batch queue, platform presets, validation, and package manifests.

evidence: README.md describes terminal-first agent-native video editing with CLI/TUI, desktop, MCP indexers, skills, and rendering.
crates/core/src/tools/apply_edl.rs provides an approval-gated structured EDL mutation path.
crates/core/src/edl/op.rs includes trim, split, insert, move, b-roll, PiP, transitions, cut intent, audio, color, LUT, title, caption, output format, loudness, and package metadata operations.
current_awidat_strengths.assessment: This is a strong foundation for agent-driven editing and is more structured than a simple timeline toy.

evidence: crates/proto/src/awidat_meta.rs stores timeline cut boundaries with SemanticCutSpec.
crates/proto/src/awidat_meta.rs stores SplitEditSpec on clip metadata.
apps/desktop/src/timeline/TimelinePane.tsx overlays cut badges and J/L split offset markers.
current_awidat_strengths.assessment: Awidat already captures the intent behind cuts and split edits, which many conventional editors do not model explicitly.

evidence: crates/effects/src/lib.rs defines graph-native Awidat effect ids for volume, speed, color correction, LUT, title, video overlay, audio fade, and audio FX.
crates/render/src/timeline.rs plans transitions, overlays, titles, audio tracks, ducking, color correction, LUTs, and split-edit audio.
current_awidat_strengths.assessment: The system already has a semantic effect registry and FFmpeg-backed lowering path.

evidence: crates/config/src/defaults.rs registers audio-energy, scenedetect, whisper, topic, editorial-moments, clip, face, shot, gaze, frame-quality, and color-analysis indexers.

python/packages/shot-mcp/src/shot_mcp/__init__.py emits edit-aware shot fields including motion, dominant direction, composition, eye trace, action score, whip pan score, occlusion score, and match candidates.
python/SMOKE.md documents safe and model-backed indexer checks.
current_awidat_strengths.assessment: Awidat is well positioned to make edit decisions from indexed evidence rather than only from timeline coordinates.

evidence: apps/desktop/src/App.tsx provides chat/transcript/edit sidebar tabs plus media, timeline, properties, and notes panes.
apps/desktop/src/app/ActionBar.tsx exposes import files, import URL, run indexers, export, permission mode, job status, proposal status, note count, and timeline status.
apps/desktop/src/properties/PropertiesPane.tsx exposes volume, fades, split edits, speed, titles, LUTs, color correction, and track mix controls.
current_awidat_strengths.assessment: The app has the right review/proposal shape for collaborative editing, but not yet the full workflow breadth of Resolve.

gaps.resolve_reference: Media Page, Media Pool, bins, metadata, import preparation
gaps.current_awidat: Imports local files and URLs, creates proxies, lists assets, stores source assets, and can index media.
missing: Editable asset metadata tags and roles
Offline/relink/proxy readiness model visible to agents
Source review workspace for sorting and selecting before timeline insertion
gaps.implementation_direction: Add an asset catalog layer separate from OTIO timeline clips. Include bins, labels, roles, provenance, proxy/indexing status, and agent-queryable selection sets.

gaps.resolve_reference: Resolve pages: Media, Cut/Edit, Fusion, Color, Fairlight, Deliver
gaps.current_awidat: Desktop uses panes rather than workflow modes. This fits agent collaboration but makes task context less explicit.
missing: Different defaults for assembly, VFX, color, audio, and delivery sessions
gaps.implementation_direction: Introduce lightweight workspace modes or task lenses without copying Resolve chrome. Modes should change available controls, prompts, and validation checklists.

gaps.resolve_reference: Inspector keyframe controls, title tracking/spacing animation, dynamic zoom, spline panel
gaps.current_awidat: Titles have a coarse animation enum. Effects are mostly static per clip. Speed, color, volume, audio fade, and title style are single values.
missing: Desktop keyframe lane or inspector controls
Render lowering for animated properties beyond fixed title presets
gaps.implementation_direction: Add a ParameterAnimation schema and support it first for title transform/text, opacity, scale, position, and volume before expanding to arbitrary effects.

gaps.resolve_reference: Fusion node graph with MediaIn, Merge, masks, transforms, trackers, MediaOut
gaps.current_awidat: Effects are graph-native in naming but stored as clip effects or timeline overlays, not as explicit compositing DAGs.
missing: Desktop node graph or compact node inspector
gaps.implementation_direction: Start with a small Awidat composition graph for overlays and tracked inserts, not a full Fusion clone. Nodes should be serializable, diffable, and lowerable to FFmpeg where possible.

gaps.resolve_reference: Basic tracker, planar tracker, surface tracker, 3D tracking, masks, mattes, magic mask
gaps.current_awidat: Shot indexer has motion, composition, face, gaze, action, whip pan, occlusion, and match scores. It does not appear to store object/planar/surface track paths or reusable mask shapes.
missing: Tracker sidecars with points/planes/surfaces and confidence
Mask shape sidecars with keyframed paths
VFX review package for track quality
gaps.implementation_direction: Add tracker/mask indexers or sidecar contracts before UI. Then add EDL operations like InsertTrackedOverlay, SetMask, and AttachEffectToTrack.

gaps.resolve_reference: Color management, grade matching, gallery stills, reset grades/nodes, LUTs, render-time surprises
gaps.current_awidat: Has color-analysis indexer, SetColorCorrection, ApplyLut, PropertiesPane color sliders, and color-corrector skill scripts.
missing: Scopes or scope-derived metrics in UI
Grade stack or node-like grade stages
Before/after contact sheets tied to proposed correction
gaps.implementation_direction: Treat color match as a review workflow: choose reference, group shots, produce recommendations, show contact sheets/scopes, then apply graph ops.

gaps.resolve_reference: Fairlight page, mixer, EQ, compression, audio repair, loudness
gaps.current_awidat: Has track audio controls, ducking, clip/track audio FX, loudness target, waveforms, and render support.
gaps.implementation_direction: Elevate existing audio primitives into a mixer task lens, with dialogue/music/SFX roles and reviewable before/after audio renders.

gaps.resolve_reference: Deliver page, export presets, render settings, render workflow
gaps.current_awidat: Has export timeline, start_render/poll_render, package metadata, output format, and platform metadata operations.
gaps.implementation_direction: Add delivery profiles as data and expose preflight checks before render: aspect, loudness, captions, safe area, missing media, render settings, and package metadata.

gaps.current_awidat: EDL operations are broad; desktop supports timeline selection, trim/move interactions, proposals, and agent chat.
missing: Timeline track controls and lane-level targeting
Assembly review workflow separate from polished edit review
gaps.implementation_direction: Keep EDL as canonical mutation path, but add direct manipulation and command palette affordances for high-frequency edit operations.

gaps.resolve_reference: Text Plus, title templates, Fusion comp duplicates, particles, 3D, write-on effects
gaps.current_awidat: Supports titles/captions and broadcast overlays; title animation options are limited.
missing: Template parameter schema agents can fill
gaps.implementation_direction: Start with reusable title/lower-third templates and parameterized text animations, then consider deeper generator nodes.

recommended_sequence.goal: Discuss which Resolve/Premiere-class capabilities define the professional editing pipeline Awidat must support before a complete autonomous editor brain can orchestrate it.
outputs: Definition of professional editor pipeline stages and required tool substrate
Definition of professional editor decisions the agent will later make autonomously
Definition of Resolve/Premiere-inspired but Awidat-native workflow modes or task lenses

recommended_sequence.goal: Add asset catalog and delivery profile data models before larger orchestration work.
Generalize keyframes and animated inspector properties.
Introduce tracker and mask sidecar contracts before attempting a node graph UI.
Turn color, audio, and delivery into review workflows with preflight reports.
After the core substrate exists, teach the agent to choose and sequence professional operations across the whole pipeline.

discussion_questions: For each Resolve/Premiere capability, should Awidat expose a manual control, an agent tool, or both?
Which professional editing pipeline components must exist before the autonomous decision layer can be reliable?
What professional editing decisions should the agent eventually make without requiring the user to know editing terminology?
Should Awidat expose Resolve-like workflow modes, or keep the current pane layout and use agent task lenses instead?
Do we want a full node graph eventually, or a smaller composition graph focused on tracked overlays, titles, masks, and reusable effects?
Should the next implementation plan prioritize media organization and delivery profiles, keyframes and motion graphics, or autonomous edit-decision planning first?
How much manual direct manipulation should the desktop gain while keeping the agent as the primary editor?
